summary.text: Max Miller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 7th District, first elected in 2022. Before Congress he served in the Marine Corps Reserve and worked on Donald Trump's 2016 campaign, in the first Trump administration, and on the 2020 re-election campaign. He serves on the Ways and Means and Foreign Affairs committees and is seeking a third term.

paragraphs.text: Miller grew up in Northeast Ohio and was born in 1988. He attended the University of Arizona from 2007 to 2009, then earned a bachelor's degree in history from Cleveland State University in 2013.
He served six years in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve, according to his House website; Wikipedia reports that he joined in 2013, rose to corporal and had no deployments.

Miller joined Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign in February 2016 after working for Marco Rubio's campaign. In the first Trump administration he held roles including confidential assistant at the Treasury Department (2017), lead advance representative in the White House, and associate director of the Presidential Personnel Office; his House website describes him as a former senior advisor to the president.
In July 2020 he was named deputy campaign manager for presidential operations on Trump's re-election campaign, and in December 2020 he was appointed to the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Council.

Miller launched a congressional campaign in February 2021. He won the May 3, 2022 Republican primary with 71.8% of the vote and the November 2022 general election over Democrat Matthew Diemer with 55.4%.
He won re-election in 2024 over Diemer and independent Dennis Kucinich, and won the 2026 Republican primary unopposed.

In Congress, Miller was chosen by fellow sophomore Republicans to serve on the Republican Steering Committee. According to his House website, he sits on the Ways and Means Committee (Oversight and Work and Welfare subcommittees) and the Foreign Affairs Committee.
In January 2023 he introduced the resolution, adopted by the House, to remove Rep. Ilhan Omar from the Foreign Affairs Committee.
He lives in Bay Village, Ohio, according to his House website.
